claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
The fcc phase is relatively soft and ductile, whereas the B2 phase is hard.
A balanced lamellar fcc/B2 structure can provide a combination of high strength and high ductility in eutectic HEAs.
Rapid solidification will lock in a refined eutectic lamellar spacing.
A brief anneal near the solidus will optimize coherent fcc/B2 interphase boundaries.
A fine-scale eutectic structure improves the distribution of hard and soft phases.
A large number of interfaces in a fine lamellar microstructure contributes to high flow stress.
Brief high-temperature annealing selectively relaxes fcc/B2 interphase boundaries.
The anneal-adjusted interphase boundaries will block dislocation motion and increase strength.
The anneal-adjusted interphase boundaries will preserve phase connectivity and thereby maintain or increase ductility.
Rapid solidification followed by brief near-solidus annealing will increase yield strength relative to conventional processing.
Rapid solidification followed by brief near-solidus annealing will increase ultimate tensile strength relative to conventional processing.
Rapid solidification followed by brief near-solidus annealing will retain or improve tensile ductility relative to conventional processing.
The proposed strength-ductility improvement should hold at room temperature for eutectic compositions having a balanced lamellar fcc/B2 structure.
Excessive annealing can cause coarsening or phase transformations that negate the mechanical-property benefits.
The magnitude of the improvement may vary with processing conditions and alloy composition.
Room-temperature tensile testing and microscopy will be used to compare the treated material with a conventionally processed control.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis calls the intervention a 'single-step process,' but the intervention consists of two sequential processing operations: rapid solidification followed by a separate annealing treatment.
